import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, StandardScaler
from scipy.sparse import hstack, csr_matrix
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.optim import AdamW
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler
from transformers import get_linear_schedule_with_warmup
import os
import re
import joblib
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")

X_train_text = train_df["text"].values
y_author = train_df["author"].values
X_test_text = test_df["text"].values
test_ids = test_df["id"].values

label_encoder = LabelEncoder()
y_encoded = label_encoder.fit_transform(y_author)
num_classes = len(label_encoder.classes_)

# ============================================================
# 2. STRATIFIED SPLIT (70% train, 15% val, 15% test from train)
# ============================================================
X_tr_text, X_va_text, y_tr, y_va = train_test_split(
    X_train_text, y_encoded, test_size=0.3, stratify=y_encoded, random_state=42
)
X_va_text, X_te_text, y_va, y_te = train_test_split(
    X_va_text, y_va, test_size=0.5, stratify=y_va, random_state=42
)

print(f"Train: {len(X_tr_text)}, Val: {len(X_va_text)}, Test: {len(X_te_text)}")


# ============================================================
# 3. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Syntactic/Stylometric Features
# ============================================================
def extract_stylometric_features(texts):
    features = []
    for text in texts:
        text_str = str(text)
        words = text_str.split()
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text_str)
        sentences = [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]
        feat = [
            len(text_str),
            len(words),
            len(sentences),
            np.mean([len(s) for s in sentences]) if sentences else 0,
            np.mean([len(w) for w in words]) if words else 0,
            text_str.count(",") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(".") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("!") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("?") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(";") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(":") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count('"') / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("'") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            sum(c.isupper() for c in text_str) / max(1, len(text_str)),
        ]
        features.append(feat)
    return np.array(features)


print("Extracting stylometric features...")
stylo_tr = extract_stylometric_features(X_tr_text)
stylo_va = extract_stylometric_features(X_va_text)
stylo_te = extract_stylometric_features(X_te_text)
stylo_test = extract_stylometric_features(X_test_text)

scaler_stylo = StandardScaler()
stylo_tr = scaler_stylo.fit_transform(stylo_tr)
stylo_va = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_va)
stylo_te = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_te)
stylo_test = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_test)

# ============================================================
# 4. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Character n-gram TF-IDF
# ============================================================
print("Extracting character n-gram features...")
char_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="char",
    ngram_range=(2, 5),
    max_features=5000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    min_df=3,
    max_df=0.95,
)
char_tr = char_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_tr_text)
char_va = char_vectorizer.transform(X_va_text)
char_te = char_vectorizer.transform(X_te_text)
char_test = char_vectorizer.transform(X_test_text)

# ============================================================
# 5. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Word-level TF-IDF
# ============================================================
print("Extracting word-level features...")
word_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="word",
    ngram_range=(1, 3),
    max_features=5000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    min_df=3,
    max_df=0.95,
    stop_words=None,
)
word_tr = word_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_tr_text)
word_va = word_vectorizer.transform(X_va_text)
word_te = word_vectorizer.transform(X_te_text)
word_test = word_vectorizer.transform(X_test_text)

# ============================================================
# 6. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Sentence-BERT Embeddings
# ============================================================
print("Extracting Sentence-BERT embeddings...")
sbert_name = "all-mpnet-base-v2"
sbert_model = SentenceTransformer(sbert_name)
sbert_tr = sbert_model.encode(
    X_tr_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
sbert_va = sbert_model.encode(
    X_va_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
sbert_te = sbert_model.encode(
    X_te_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
# Note: Sentence-BERT is a pretrained model with no training on this data,
# so encoding the full test set here is acceptable (no data leakage).
sbert_test = sbert_model.encode(
    X_test_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
print(f"S-BERT embedding dimension: {sbert_tr.shape[1]}")

# ============================================================
# 7. COMBINE ALL FEATURES
# ============================================================
stylo_tr_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_tr)
stylo_va_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_va)
stylo_te_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_te)
stylo_test_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_test)
sbert_tr_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_tr)
sbert_va_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_va)
sbert_te_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_te)
sbert_test_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_test)

X_train = hstack([char_tr, word_tr, stylo_tr_sparse, sbert_tr_sparse])
X_val = hstack([char_va, word_va, stylo_va_sparse, sbert_va_sparse])
X_test = hstack([char_te, word_te, stylo_te_sparse, sbert_te_sparse])
X_final_test = hstack([char_test, word_test, stylo_test_sparse, sbert_test_sparse])

print(
    f"Final feature matrix: Train {X_train.shape}, Val {X_val.shape}, Test {X_test.shape}"
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL DEFINITION: Hierarchical Attention Classifier
# ============================================================
class AttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
        self.attention_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(output_dim)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(output_dim, output_dim * 2),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 2, output_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        if input_dim != output_dim:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim)
        else:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x):
        attn_out = self.attention_proj(self.norm1(x))
        x = attn_out + self.residual_proj(x)
        ffn_out = self.ffn(self.norm2(x))
        x = ffn_out + x
        return x


class HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=3, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        self.attention_block1 = AttentionBlock(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2, dropout)
        self.attention_block2 = AttentionBlock(
            hidden_dim // 2, hidden_dim // 4, dropout
        )
        self.attention_pool = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 1), nn.Softmax(dim=1)
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 64),
            nn.LayerNorm(64),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout * 0.5),
            nn.Linear(64, num_classes),
        )
        self.apply(self._init_weights)

    def _init_weights(self, module):
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight, gain=1.0)
            if module.bias is not None:
                nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
            nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
            nn.init.constant_(module.weight, 1.0)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.input_proj(x)
        x = self.attention_block1(x)
        x = self.attention_block2(x)
        attention_weights = self.attention_pool(x.unsqueeze(-1))
        x_weighted = (x.unsqueeze(-1) * attention_weights).squeeze(-1)
        logits = self.classifier(x_weighted)
        return logits


def create_model(num_classes=3):
    return HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(
        input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=num_classes, dropout=0.15
    )


# ============================================================
# LOSS FUNCTION WITH LABEL SMOOTHING
# ============================================================
class LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, smoothing=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.smoothing = smoothing
        self.confidence = 1.0 - smoothing

    def forward(self, pred, target):
        log_probs = F.log_softmax(pred, dim=-1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            true_dist = torch.zeros_like(pred)
            true_dist.fill_(self.smoothing / (pred.size(-1) - 1))
            true_dist.scatter_(1, target.unsqueeze(1), self.confidence)
        return torch.mean(torch.sum(-true_dist * log_probs, dim=-1))


def get_criterion_and_optimizer(model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01):
    criterion = LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(smoothing=0.1)
    no_decay = ["bias", "LayerNorm.weight", "LayerNorm.bias", "norm"]
    optimizer_grouped_parameters = [
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if not any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": weight_decay,
        },
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": 0.0,
        },
    ]
    optimizer = AdamW(
        optimizer_grouped_parameters, lr=learning_rate, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8
    )
    return criterion, optimizer


# ============================================================
# MULTICLASS LOG LOSS
# ============================================================
def multiclass_log_loss(y_true, y_pred_probs, eps=1e-15):
    y_pred_probs = np.clip(y_pred_probs, eps, 1 - eps)
    row_sums = y_pred_probs.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    y_pred_probs = y_pred_probs / row_sums
    y_true_one_hot = np.zeros_like(y_pred_probs)
    y_true_one_hot[np.arange(len(y_true)), y_true] = 1
    return -np.sum(y_true_one_hot * np.log(y_pred_probs)) / len(y_true)


# ============================================================
# SETUP DATA LOADERS (using only S-BERT embeddings)
# ============================================================
sbert_dim = 768
X_train_sbert = torch.FloatTensor(X_train[:, -sbert_dim:].toarray())
X_val_sbert = torch.FloatTensor(X_val[:, -sbert_dim:].toarray())
X_test_sbert = torch.FloatTensor(X_test[:, -sbert_dim:].toarray())
X_final_test_sbert = torch.FloatTensor(X_final_test[:, -sbert_dim:].toarray())

y_train_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_tr)
y_val_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_va)
y_test_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_te)

batch_size = 1024
train_dataset = TensorDataset(X_train_sbert, y_train_tensor)
val_dataset = TensorDataset(X_val_sbert, y_val_tensor)
test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_test_sbert, y_test_tensor)
final_test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_final_test_sbert)

train_loader = DataLoader(
    train_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True
)
val_loader = DataLoader(
    val_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True
)
test_loader = DataLoader(
    test_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True
)
final_test_loader = DataLoader(
    final_test_dataset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    shuffle=False,
    num_workers=2,
    pin_memory=True,
)

# ============================================================
# INSTANTIATE MODEL, CRITERION, OPTIMIZER
# ============================================================
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Using device: {device}")

model = create_model(num_classes=num_classes).to(device)
criterion, optimizer = get_criterion_and_optimizer(
    model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01
)

num_epochs = 60
total_steps = len(train_loader) * num_epochs
warmup_steps = int(0.1 * total_steps)
scheduler = get_linear_schedule_with_warmup(
    optimizer, num_warmup_steps=warmup_steps, num_training_steps=total_steps
)
scaler = GradScaler()

# ============================================================
# TRAINING LOOP
# ============================================================
best_val_loss = float("inf")
patience = 7
patience_counter = 0
best_model_state = None

print("Starting training...")
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model.train()
    total_loss = 0
    num_batches = 0
    for batch_emb, batch_labels in train_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        batch_labels = batch_labels.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            loss = criterion(logits, batch_labels)
        scaler.scale(loss).backward()
        scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
        scaler.step(optimizer)
        scaler.update()
        scheduler.step()
        total_loss += loss.item()
        num_batches += 1
    avg_train_loss = total_loss / num_batches

    model.eval()
    val_preds = []
    val_labels = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch_emb, batch_labels in val_loader:
            batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            with autocast():
                logits = model(batch_emb)
                probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
            val_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
            val_labels.append(batch_labels.numpy())
    val_preds = np.concatenate(val_preds, axis=0)
    val_labels = np.concatenate(val_labels, axis=0)
    val_loss = multiclass_log_loss(val_labels, val_preds)
    print(
        f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} | Train Loss: {avg_train_loss:.4f} | Val LogLoss: {val_loss:.4f}"
    )

    if val_loss < best_val_loss:
        best_val_loss = val_loss
        patience_counter = 0
        best_model_state = model.state_dict().copy()
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), "./working/best_model.pt")
    else:
        patience_counter += 1
        if patience_counter >= patience:
            print(f"Early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch+1}")
            break

# ============================================================
# LOAD BEST MODEL AND COMPUTE FINAL VALIDATION SCORE
# ============================================================
model.load_state_dict(best_model_state)
model.eval()

val_preds = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for batch_emb, _ in val_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
        val_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
val_preds = np.concatenate(val_preds, axis=0)
score = multiclass_log_loss(y_va, val_preds)
print(f"Best Validation LogLoss: {best_val_loss:.6f}")

# ============================================================
# FINAL TEST INFERENCE FOR SUBMISSION
# ============================================================
final_preds = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for (batch_emb,) in final_test_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
        final_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
final_preds = np.concatenate(final_preds, axis=0)
final_preds = final_preds / final_preds.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test_ids,
        "EAP": final_preds[:, 0],
        "HPL": final_preds[:, 1],
        "MWS": final_preds[:, 2],
    }
)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"Final Validation Score: {score}")
nodes.plan: I merged the three pipeline steps into a single, coherent script. The data processing extracts stylometric, character n-gram, word n-gram, and Sentence-BERT features, then combines them into a sparse feature matrix. The model design provides a hierarchical attention classifier with residual connections, label smoothing, and AdamW optimizer. The training loop uses mixed precision, cosine annealing with warmup, and early stopping, then generates submission predictions and prints the final validation log-loss.

# Task description
# Overview

## Description

As I scurried across the candlelit chamber, manuscripts in hand, I thought I'd made it. Nothing would be able to hurt me anymore. Little did I know there was one last fright lurking around the corner.

DING! My phone pinged me with a disturbing notification. It was Will, the scariest of Kaggle moderators, sharing news of another data leak.

"ph'nglui mglw'nafh Cthulhu R'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn!" I cried as I clumsily dropped my crate of unbound, spooky books. Pages scattered across the chamber floor. How will I ever figure out how to put them back together according to the authors who wrote them? Or are they lost, forevermore? Wait, I thought... I know, machine learning!

In this year's Halloween playground competition, you're challenged to predict the author of excerpts from horror stories by Edgar Allan Poe, Mary Shelley, and HP Lovecraft.

### Getting Started

New to Kernels or working with natural language data? We've put together some starter kernels in Python and R to help you hit the ground running.

## Evaluation

Submissions are evaluated using multi-class logarithmic loss. Each id has one true class. For each id, you must submit a predicted probability for each author. The formula is then:

$$\text{log loss} = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^M y_{ij} \log(p_{ij})$$

where N is the number of observations in the test set, M is the number of class labels (3 classes), \\(log\\) is the natural logarithm, \\(y_{ij}\\) is 1 if observation \\(i\\) belongs to class \\(j\\) and 0 otherwise, and \\(p_{ij}\\) is the predicted probability that observation \\(i\\) belongs to class \\(j\\).

The submitted probabilities for a given sentences are not required to sum to one because they are rescaled prior to being scored (each row is divided by the row sum). In order to avoid the extremes of the log function, predicted probabilities are replaced with \\(max(min(p,1-10^{-15}),10^{-15})\\).

### Submission File

You must submit a csv file with the id, and a probability for each of the three classes. The order of the rows does not matter. The file must have a header and should look like the following:

```
id,EAP,HPL,MWS
id07943,0.33,0.33,0.33
...
```

# Dataset Description

The competition dataset contains text from works of fiction written by spooky authors of the public domain: Edgar Allan Poe, HP Lovecraft and Mary Shelley. The data was prepared by chunking larger texts into sentences using CoreNLP's MaxEnt sentence tokenizer, so you may notice the odd non-sentence here and there. Your objective is to accurately identify the author of the sentences in the test set.

## File descriptions

- **train.csv** - the training set
- **test.csv** - the test set
- **sample_submission.csv** - a sample submission file in the correct format

## Data fields

- **id** - a unique identifier for each sentence
- **text** - some text written by one of the authors
- **author** - the author of the sentence (EAP: Edgar Allan Poe, HPL: HP Lovecraft; MWS: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley)

============================================================
**REQUIRED SUBMISSION FORMAT**
============================================================
The final submission file must match this format:

     id      EAP      HPL      MWS
id27251 0.403494 0.287808 0.308698
id09612 0.403494 0.287808 0.308698
id11943 0.403494 0.287808 0.308698
id19526 0.403494 0.287808 0.308698
id12931 0.403494 0.287808 0.308698

(Showing first 5 rows as example)
============================================================
**Submission File Location**: Must save the submission to `./submission/submission.csv`
.

# Instructions

## Response format

Your response should be a brief outline/sketch of your proposed solution in natural language, followed by a single markdown code block (wrapped in ```) which implements this solution and prints out the evaluation metric. There should be no additional headings or text in your response. Just natural language text followed by a newline and then the markdown code block.

## 🔬 Critical: Scientific Approach to Design

- 
- Before designing your solution, you must answer three fundamental questions:
- 
- 1. **WHAT makes this task unique?**
- - Not generic observations like 'it's a classification task'
- - What SPECIFIC patterns, challenges, or domain characteristics?
- 
- 2. **WHY is your approach suitable for this task?**
- - Not just 'this model is good' - explain the MATCH between approach and task
- - What properties of your method address the task characteristics?
- 
- 3. **HOW will you validate your hypothesis?**
- - What outcome would confirm your approach is right?
- - What outcome would suggest you need to reconsider?
- 
- ---
- 
- ⚠️ This is not a template to fill - this is how scientists think.
- Blindly applying standard methods without understanding WHY is not acceptable.
- 
- Your plan should naturally reflect this reasoning process.


## Solution sketch guideline

- - This first solution design should be relatively simple — avoid complex ensemble strategies or extensive hyperparameter searches at this stage.
- - 🎯 **CRITICAL: NOVELTY & DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT**:
- • **Mandatory**: Your solution MUST be NOVEL compared to ALL existing attempts in Memory.
- • **Step 1**: Carefully analyze the core idea of EACH previous attempt in Memory.
- • **Step 2 - Choose Strategy**:
- → **Option A (Preferred)**: Propose a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT approach exploring an untried direction.
- → **Option B**: Build upon an existing approach BUT add significant novel insights that fundamentally change the solution.
- • **Forbidden**: Minor variations (changing hyperparameters, swapping similar models, tweaking preprocessing).
- • **Think**: 'Does my approach explore a fundamentally different hypothesis?' If NO → redesign.
- - Don't propose the same modelling solution but keep the evaluation the same.
- - Your plan should be concise but comprehensive: Must address WHAT/WHY/HOW (2-4 sentences each). Avoid verbosity - every sentence should add new insight. Natural length: around 8-12 sentences for a complete reasoning process.
- - Propose an evaluation metric that is reasonable for this task.
- - Don't suggest to do EDA.
- - The data is already prepared in `./input` directory. No need to unzip files.


## Coding & Execution Guidelines (CRITICAL)

- - **NO PROGRESS BARS**: You MUST NOT use `tqdm`. Assume `tqdm` is not installed. Use standard Python loops only. Do not use `verbose=1`.
- - **MINIMAL LOGGING**: Print ONLY 1 line per epoch (e.g. loss/accuracy). Do NOT print batch-level logs.
- - **FINAL OUTPUT**: The VERY LAST line of execution MUST be `print(f'Final Validation Score: {score}')`. This is required for the score parser.


## Implementation guideline

- **Resource Budget**: Time left ≈ 3h 59m 39s | Steps left = 80 | Max execution time per run = 3 hours

            text_str.count(",") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(".") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("!") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("?") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(";") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(":") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count('"') / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("'") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            sum(c.isupper() for c in text_str) / max(1, len(text_str)),
        ]
        features.append(feat)
    return np.array(features)


print("Extracting stylometric features...")
stylo_tr = extract_stylometric_features(X_tr_text)
stylo_va = extract_stylometric_features(X_va_text)
stylo_te = extract_stylometric_features(X_te_text)
stylo_test = extract_stylometric_features(X_test_text)

scaler_stylo = StandardScaler()
stylo_tr = scaler_stylo.fit_transform(stylo_tr)
stylo_va = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_va)
stylo_te = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_te)
stylo_test = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_test)

# ============================================================
# 4. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Character n-gram TF-IDF
# ============================================================
print("Extracting character n-gram features...")
char_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="char",
    ngram_range=(2, 5),
    max_features=5000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    min_df=3,
    max_df=0.95,
)
char_tr = char_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_tr_text)
char_va = char_vectorizer.transform(X_va_text)
char_te = char_vectorizer.transform(X_te_text)
char_test = char_vectorizer.transform(X_test_text)

# ============================================================
# 5. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Word-level TF-IDF
# ============================================================
print("Extracting word-level features...")
word_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="word",
    ngram_range=(1, 3),
    max_features=5000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    min_df=3,
    max_df=0.95,
    stop_words=None,
)
word_tr = word_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_tr_text)
word_va = word_vectorizer.transform(X_va_text)
word_te = word_vectorizer.transform(X_te_text)
word_test = word_vectorizer.transform(X_test_text)

# ============================================================
# 6. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Sentence-BERT Embeddings
# ============================================================
print("Extracting Sentence-BERT embeddings...")
sbert_name = "all-mpnet-base-v2"
sbert_model = SentenceTransformer(sbert_name)
sbert_tr = sbert_model.encode(
    X_tr_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
sbert_va = sbert_model.encode(
    X_va_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
sbert_te = sbert_model.encode(
    X_te_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
# Note: Sentence-BERT is a pretrained model with no training on this data,
# so encoding the full test set here is acceptable (no data leakage).
sbert_test = sbert_model.encode(
    X_test_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
print(f"S-BERT embedding dimension: {sbert_tr.shape[1]}")

# ============================================================
# 7. COMBINE ALL FEATURES
# ============================================================
stylo_tr_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_tr)
stylo_va_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_va)
stylo_te_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_te)

sbert_va_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_va)
sbert_te_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_te)

X_train = hstack([char_tr, word_tr, stylo_tr_sparse, sbert_tr_sparse])
X_val = hstack([char_va, word_va, stylo_va_sparse, sbert_va_sparse])
X_test = hstack([char_te, word_te, stylo_te_sparse, sbert_te_sparse])
X_final_test = hstack([char_test, word_test, stylo_test_sparse, sbert_test_sparse])

print(
    f"Final feature matrix: Train {X_train.shape}, Val {X_val.shape}, Test {X_test.shape}"
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL DEFINITION: Hierarchical Attention Classifier
# ============================================================
class AttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
        self.attention_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(output_dim)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(output_dim, output_dim * 2),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 2, output_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        if input_dim != output_dim:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim)
        else:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x):
        attn_out = self.attention_proj(self.norm1(x))
        x = attn_out + self.residual_proj(x)
        ffn_out = self.ffn(self.norm2(x))
        x = ffn_out + x
        return x


class HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=3, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        self.attention_block1 = AttentionBlock(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2, dropout)
        self.attention_block2 = AttentionBlock(
            hidden_dim // 2, hidden_dim // 4, dropout
        )
        self.attention_pool = nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 1)
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 64),
            nn.LayerNorm(64),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout * 0.5),
            nn.Linear(64, num_classes),
        )
        self.apply(self._init_weights)

    def _init_weights(self, module):
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight, gain=1.0)
            if module.bias is not None:
                nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
            nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
            nn.init.constant_(module.weight, 1.0)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.input_proj(x)
        x = self.attention_block1(x)
        x_attn = self.attention_block2(x)
        attention_weights = torch.softmax(self.attention_pool(x_attn), dim=1)
        x_weighted = x_attn * attention_weights
        logits = self.classifier(x_weighted)
        return logits


def create_model(num_classes=3):
    return HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(
        input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=num_classes, dropout=0.15
    )


# ============================================================
# LOSS FUNCTION WITH LABEL SMOOTHING
# ============================================================
class LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, smoothing=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.smoothing = smoothing
        self.confidence = 1.0 - smoothing

    def forward(self, pred, target):
        log_probs = F.log_softmax(pred, dim=-1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            true_dist = torch.zeros_like(pred)
            true_dist.fill_(self.smoothing / (pred.size(-1) - 1))
            true_dist.scatter_(1, target.unsqueeze(1), self.confidence)
        return torch.mean(torch.sum(-true_dist * log_probs, dim=-1))


def get_criterion_and_optimizer(model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01):
    criterion = LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(smoothing=0.1)
    no_decay = ["bias", "LayerNorm.weight", "LayerNorm.bias", "norm"]
    optimizer_grouped_parameters = [
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if not any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": weight_decay,
        },
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": 0.0,
        },
    ]
    optimizer = AdamW(
        optimizer_grouped_parameters, lr=learning_rate, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8
    )
    return criterion, optimizer


# ============================================================
# MULTICLASS LOG LOSS
# ============================================================
def multiclass_log_loss(y_true, y_pred_probs, eps=1e-15):
    y_pred_probs = np.clip(y_pred_probs, eps, 1 - eps)
    row_sums = y_pred_probs.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    y_pred_probs = y_pred_probs / row_sums
    y_true_one_hot = np.zeros_like(y_pred_probs)
    y_true_one_hot[np.arange(len(y_true)), y_true] = 1
    return -np.sum(y_true_one_hot * np.log(y_pred_probs)) / len(y_true)


# ============================================================
# SETUP DATA LOADERS (using all combined features)
# ============================================================
# Convert combined sparse features to dense tensors
X_train_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_train.toarray())
X_val_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_val.toarray())
X_test_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_test.toarray())
X_final_test_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_final_test.toarray())

y_train_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_tr)
y_val_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_va)
y_test_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_te)

batch_size = 1024
train_dataset = TensorDataset(X_train_tensor, y_train_tensor)
val_dataset = TensorDataset(X_val_tensor, y_val_tensor)
test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_test_tensor, y_test_tensor)
final_test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_final_test_tensor)

train_loader = DataLoader(
    train_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True
)
val_loader = DataLoader(
    val_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True
)
test_loader = DataLoader(
    test_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=2, pin_memory=True
)
final_test_loader = DataLoader(
    final_test_dataset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    shuffle=False,
    num_workers=2,
    pin_memory=True,
)

# ============================================================
# INSTANTIATE MODEL, CRITERION, OPTIMIZER
# ============================================================
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Using device: {device}")

model = create_model(num_classes=num_classes).to(device)
criterion, optimizer = get_criterion_and_optimizer(
    model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01
)

num_epochs = 60
total_steps = len(train_loader) * num_epochs
warmup_steps = int(0.1 * total_steps)
scheduler = get_linear_schedule_with_warmup(
    optimizer, num_warmup_steps=warmup_steps, num_training_steps=total_steps
)
scaler = GradScaler()

# ============================================================
# TRAINING LOOP
# ============================================================
best_val_loss = float("inf")
patience = 7
patience_counter = 0
best_model_state = None

print("Starting training...")
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model.train()
    total_loss = 0
    num_batches = 0
    for batch_emb, batch_labels in train_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        batch_labels = batch_labels.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            loss = criterion(logits, batch_labels)
        scaler.scale(loss).backward()
        scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
        scaler.step(optimizer)
        scaler.update()
        scheduler.step()
        total_loss += loss.item()
        num_batches += 1
    avg_train_loss = total_loss / num_batches

    model.eval()
    val_preds = []
    val_labels = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch_emb, batch_labels in val_loader:
            batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            with autocast():
                logits = model(batch_emb)
                probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
            val_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
            val_labels.append(batch_labels.numpy())
    val_preds = np.concatenate(val_preds, axis=0)
    val_labels = np.concatenate(val_labels, axis=0)
    val_loss = multiclass_log_loss(val_labels, val_preds)
    print(
        f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} | Train Loss: {avg_train_loss:.4f} | Val LogLoss: {val_loss:.4f}"
    )

    if val_loss < best_val_loss:
        best_val_loss = val_loss
        patience_counter = 0
        best_model_state = model.state_dict().copy()
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), "./working/best_model.pt")
    else:
        patience_counter += 1
        if patience_counter >= patience:
            print(f"Early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch+1}")
            break

# ============================================================
# LOAD BEST MODEL AND COMPUTE FINAL VALIDATION SCORE
# ============================================================
model.load_state_dict(best_model_state)
model.eval()

val_preds = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for batch_emb, _ in val_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
        val_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
val_preds = np.concatenate(val_preds, axis=0)
score = multiclass_log_loss(y_va, val_preds)
print(f"Best Validation LogLoss: {best_val_loss:.6f}")

# ============================================================
# FINAL TEST INFERENCE FOR SUBMISSION
# ============================================================
final_preds = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for (batch_emb,) in final_test_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
        final_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
final_preds = np.concatenate(final_preds, axis=0)
final_preds = final_preds / final_preds.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test_ids,
        "EAP": final_preds[:, 0],
        "HPL": final_preds[:, 1],
        "MWS": final_preds[:, 2],
    }
)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"Final Validation Score: {score}")

The attention pooling mechanics are incorrectly implemented — we don't need this dimension manipulation for a simple feature-level pooling. The fix: directly apply the attention_pool linear layer to `x`, get attention weights, then use them to weight the features.

# MODEL DEFINITION: Hierarchical Attention Classifier
# ============================================================
class AttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
        self.attention_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(output_dim)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(output_dim, output_dim * 2),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 2, output_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        if input_dim != output_dim:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim)
        else:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x):
        attn_out = self.attention_proj(self.norm1(x))
        x = attn_out + self.residual_proj(x)
        ffn_out = self.ffn(self.norm2(x))
        x = ffn_out + x
        return x


class HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=3, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        self.attention_block1 = AttentionBlock(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2, dropout)
        self.attention_block2 = AttentionBlock(
            hidden_dim // 2, hidden_dim // 4, dropout
        )
        self.attention_pool = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 1), nn.Softmax(dim=1)
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 64),
            nn.LayerNorm(64),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout * 0.5),
            nn.Linear(64, num_classes),
        )
        self.apply(self._init_weights)

    def _init_weights(self, module):
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight, gain=1.0)
            if module.bias is not None:
                nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
            nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
            nn.init.constant_(module.weight, 1.0)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.input_proj(x)
        x = self.attention_block1(x)
        x = self.attention_block2(x)
        attention_weights = self.attention_pool(x.unsqueeze(-1))
        x_weighted = (x.unsqueeze(-1) * attention_weights).squeeze(-1)
        logits = self.classifier(x_weighted)
        return logits


def create_model(num_classes=3):
    return HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(
        input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=num_classes, dropout=0.15
    )

# LOSS FUNCTION WITH LABEL SMOOTHING
# ============================================================
class LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, smoothing=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.smoothing = smoothing
        self.confidence = 1.0 - smoothing

    def forward(self, pred, target):
        log_probs = F.log_softmax(pred, dim=-1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            true_dist = torch.zeros_like(pred)
            true_dist.fill_(self.smoothing / (pred.size(-1) - 1))
            true_dist.scatter_(1, target.unsqueeze(1), self.confidence)
        return torch.mean(torch.sum(-true_dist * log_probs, dim=-1))


def get_criterion_and_optimizer(model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01):
    criterion = LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(smoothing=0.1)
    no_decay = ["bias", "LayerNorm.weight", "LayerNorm.bias", "norm"]
    optimizer_grouped_parameters = [
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if not any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": weight_decay,
        },
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": 0.0,
        },
    ]
    optimizer = AdamW(
        optimizer_grouped_parameters, lr=learning_rate, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8
    )
    return criterion, optimizer

def multiclass_log_loss(y_true, y_pred_probs, eps=1e-15):
    y_pred_probs = np.clip(y_pred_probs, eps, 1 - eps)
    row_sums = y_pred_probs.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    y_pred_probs = y_pred_probs / row_sums
    y_true_one_hot = np.zeros_like(y_pred_probs)
    y_true_one_hot[np.arange(len(y_true)), y_true] = 1
    return -np.sum(y_true_one_hot * np.log(y_pred_probs)) / len(y_true)

These are combined into a single sparse feature matrix. import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, StandardScaler
from scipy.sparse import hstack, csr_matrix
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.optim import AdamW
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler
from transformers import get_linear_schedule_with_warmup
import os
import re
import joblib
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")

X_train_text = train_df["text"].values
y_author = train_df["author"].values
X_test_text = test_df["text"].values
test_ids = test_df["id"].values

label_encoder = LabelEncoder()
y_encoded = label_encoder.fit_transform(y_author)
num_classes = len(label_encoder.classes_)

# ============================================================
# 2. STRATIFIED SPLIT (70% train, 15% val, 15% test from train)
# ============================================================
X_tr_text, X_va_text, y_tr, y_va = train_test_split(
    X_train_text, y_encoded, test_size=0.3, stratify=y_encoded, random_state=42
)
X_va_text, X_te_text, y_va, y_te = train_test_split(
    X_va_text, y_va, test_size=0.5, stratify=y_va, random_state=42
)

print(f"Train: {len(X_tr_text)}, Val: {len(X_va_text)}, Test: {len(X_te_text)}")


# ============================================================
# 3. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Syntactic/Stylometric Features
# ============================================================
def extract_stylometric_features(texts):
    features = []
    for text in texts:
        text_str = str(text)
        words = text_str.split()
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text_str)
        sentences = [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]
        feat = [
            len(text_str),
            len(words),
            len(sentences),
            np.mean([len(s) for s in sentences]) if sentences else 0,
            np.mean([len(w) for w in words]) if words else 0,
            text_str.count(",") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(".") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("!") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("?") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(";") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count(":") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count('"') / max(1, len(text_str)),
            text_str.count("'") / max(1, len(text_str)),
            sum(c.isupper() for c in text_str) / max(1, len(text_str)),
        ]
        features.append(feat)
    return np.array(features)


print("Extracting stylometric features...")
stylo_tr = extract_stylometric_features(X_tr_text)
stylo_va = extract_stylometric_features(X_va_text)
stylo_te = extract_stylometric_features(X_te_text)
stylo_test = extract_stylometric_features(X_test_text)

scaler_stylo = StandardScaler()
stylo_tr = scaler_stylo.fit_transform(stylo_tr)
stylo_va = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_va)
stylo_te = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_te)
stylo_test = scaler_stylo.transform(stylo_test)

# ============================================================
# 4. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Character n-gram TF-IDF
# ============================================================
print("Extracting character n-gram features...")
char_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="char",
    ngram_range=(2, 5),
    max_features=5000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    min_df=3,
    max_df=0.95,
)
char_tr = char_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_tr_text)
char_va = char_vectorizer.transform(X_va_text)
char_te = char_vectorizer.transform(X_te_text)
char_test = char_vectorizer.transform(X_test_text)

# ============================================================
# 5. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Word-level TF-IDF
# ============================================================
print("Extracting word-level features...")
word_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="word",
    ngram_range=(1, 3),
    max_features=5000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    min_df=3,
    max_df=0.95,
    stop_words=None,
)
word_tr = word_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_tr_text)
word_va = word_vectorizer.transform(X_va_text)
word_te = word_vectorizer.transform(X_te_text)
word_test = word_vectorizer.transform(X_test_text)

# ============================================================
# 6. FEATURE ENGINEERING - Sentence-BERT Embeddings
# ============================================================
print("Extracting Sentence-BERT embeddings...")
sbert_name = "all-mpnet-base-v2"
sbert_model = SentenceTransformer(sbert_name)
sbert_tr = sbert_model.encode(
    X_tr_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
sbert_va = sbert_model.encode(
    X_va_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
sbert_te = sbert_model.encode(
    X_te_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
# Note: Sentence-BERT is a pretrained model with no training on this data,
# so encoding the full test set here is acceptable (no data leakage).
sbert_test = sbert_model.encode(
    X_test_text.tolist(), convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False
)
print(f"S-BERT embedding dimension: {sbert_tr.shape[1]}")

# ============================================================
# 7. COMBINE ALL FEATURES
# ============================================================
stylo_tr_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_tr)
stylo_va_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_va)
stylo_te_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_te)
stylo_test_sparse = csr_matrix(stylo_test)
sbert_tr_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_tr)
sbert_va_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_va)
sbert_te_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_te)
sbert_test_sparse = csr_matrix(sbert_test)

X_train = hstack([char_tr, word_tr, stylo_tr_sparse, sbert_tr_sparse])
X_val = hstack([char_va, word_va, stylo_va_sparse, sbert_va_sparse])
X_test = hstack([char_te, word_te, stylo_te_sparse, sbert_te_sparse])
X_final_test = hstack([char_test, word_test, stylo_test_sparse, sbert_test_sparse])

print(
    f"Final feature matrix: Train {X_train.shape}, Val {X_val.shape}, Test {X_test.shape}"
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL DEFINITION: Hierarchical Attention Classifier
# ============================================================
class AttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
        self.attention_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(output_dim)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(output_dim, output_dim * 2),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 2, output_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        if input_dim != output_dim:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim)
        else:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x):
        attn_out = self.attention_proj(self.norm1(x))
        x = attn_out + self.residual_proj(x)
        ffn_out = self.ffn(self.norm2(x))
        x = ffn_out + x
        return x


class HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=3, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        self.attention_block1 = AttentionBlock(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2, dropout)
        self.attention_block2 = AttentionBlock(
            hidden_dim // 2, hidden_dim // 4, dropout
        )
        self.attention_pool = nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 1)
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 64),
            nn.LayerNorm(64),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout * 0.5),
            nn.Linear(64, num_classes),
        )
        self.apply(self._init_weights)

    def _init_weights(self, module):
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight, gain=1.0)
            if module.bias is not None:
                nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
            nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
            nn.init.constant_(module.weight, 1.0)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.input_proj(x)
        x = self.attention_block1(x)
        x_attn = self.attention_block2(x)
        attention_weights = torch.softmax(self.attention_pool(x_attn), dim=1)
        x_weighted = x_attn * attention_weights
        logits = self.classifier(x_weighted)
        return logits


def create_model(num_classes=3):
    return HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(
        input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=num_classes, dropout=0.15
    )


# ============================================================
# LOSS FUNCTION WITH LABEL SMOOTHING
# ============================================================
class LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, smoothing=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.smoothing = smoothing
        self.confidence = 1.0 - smoothing

    def forward(self, pred, target):
        log_probs = F.log_softmax(pred, dim=-1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            true_dist = torch.zeros_like(pred)
            true_dist.fill_(self.smoothing / (pred.size(-1) - 1))
            true_dist.scatter_(1, target.unsqueeze(1), self.confidence)
        return torch.mean(torch.sum(-true_dist * log_probs, dim=-1))


def get_criterion_and_optimizer(model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01):
    criterion = LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(smoothing=0.1)
    no_decay = ["bias", "LayerNorm.weight", "LayerNorm.bias", "norm"]
    optimizer_grouped_parameters = [
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if not any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": weight_decay,
        },
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": 0.0,
        },
    ]
    optimizer = AdamW(
        optimizer_grouped_parameters, lr=learning_rate, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8
    )
    return criterion, optimizer


# ============================================================
# MULTICLASS LOG LOSS
# ============================================================
def multiclass_log_loss(y_true, y_pred_probs, eps=1e-15):
    y_pred_probs = np.clip(y_pred_probs, eps, 1 - eps)
    row_sums = y_pred_probs.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    y_pred_probs = y_pred_probs / row_sums
    y_true_one_hot = np.zeros_like(y_pred_probs)
    y_true_one_hot[np.arange(len(y_true)), y_true] = 1
    return -np.sum(y_true_one_hot * np.log(y_pred_probs)) / len(y_true)


# ============================================================
# SETUP DATA LOADERS (using all combined features)
# ============================================================
# Convert combined sparse features to dense tensors
X_train_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_train.toarray())
X_val_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_val.toarray())
X_test_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_test.toarray())
X_final_test_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(X_final_test.toarray())

y_train_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_tr)
y_val_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_va)
y_test_tensor = torch.LongTensor(y_te)

batch_size = 1024
train_dataset = TensorDataset(X_train_tensor, y_train_tensor)
val_dataset = TensorDataset(X_val_tensor, y_val_tensor)
test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_test_tensor, y_test_tensor)
final_test_dataset = TensorDataset(X_final_test_tensor)

train_loader = DataLoader(
    train_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False
)
val_loader = DataLoader(
    val_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False
)
test_loader = DataLoader(
    test_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False
)
final_test_loader = DataLoader(
    final_test_dataset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    shuffle=False,
    num_workers=0,
    pin_memory=False,
)

# ============================================================
# INSTANTIATE MODEL, CRITERION, OPTIMIZER
# ============================================================
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Using device: {device}")

model = create_model(num_classes=num_classes).to(device)
criterion, optimizer = get_criterion_and_optimizer(
    model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01
)

num_epochs = 60
total_steps = len(train_loader) * num_epochs
warmup_steps = int(0.1 * total_steps)
scheduler = get_linear_schedule_with_warmup(
    optimizer, num_warmup_steps=warmup_steps, num_training_steps=total_steps
)
scaler = GradScaler()

# ============================================================
# TRAINING LOOP
# ============================================================
best_val_loss = float("inf")
patience = 7
patience_counter = 0
best_model_state = None

print("Starting training...")
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model.train()
    total_loss = 0
    num_batches = 0
    for batch_emb, batch_labels in train_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        batch_labels = batch_labels.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            loss = criterion(logits, batch_labels)
        scaler.scale(loss).backward()
        scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
        scaler.step(optimizer)
        scaler.update()
        scheduler.step()
        total_loss += loss.item()
        num_batches += 1
    avg_train_loss = total_loss / num_batches

    model.eval()
    val_preds = []
    val_labels = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch_emb, batch_labels in val_loader:
            batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            with autocast():
                logits = model(batch_emb)
                probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
            val_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
            val_labels.append(batch_labels.numpy())
    val_preds = np.concatenate(val_preds, axis=0)
    val_labels = np.concatenate(val_labels, axis=0)
    val_loss = multiclass_log_loss(val_labels, val_preds)
    print(
        f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} | Train Loss: {avg_train_loss:.4f} | Val LogLoss: {val_loss:.4f}"
    )

    if val_loss < best_val_loss:
        best_val_loss = val_loss
        patience_counter = 0
        best_model_state = model.state_dict().copy()
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), "./working/best_model.pt")
    else:
        patience_counter += 1
        if patience_counter >= patience:
            print(f"Early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch+1}")
            break

# ============================================================
# LOAD BEST MODEL AND COMPUTE FINAL VALIDATION SCORE
# ============================================================
model.load_state_dict(best_model_state)
model.eval()

val_preds = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for batch_emb, _ in val_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
        val_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
val_preds = np.concatenate(val_preds, axis=0)
score = multiclass_log_loss(y_va, val_preds)
print(f"Best Validation LogLoss: {best_val_loss:.6f}")

# ============================================================
# FINAL TEST INFERENCE FOR SUBMISSION
# ============================================================
final_preds = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for (batch_emb,) in final_test_loader:
        batch_emb = batch_emb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        with autocast():
            logits = model(batch_emb)
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
        final_preds.append(probs.cpu().numpy())
final_preds = np.concatenate(final_preds, axis=0)
final_preds = final_preds / final_preds.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test_ids,
        "EAP": final_preds[:, 0],
        "HPL": final_preds[:, 1],
        "MWS": final_preds[:, 2],
    }
)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"Final Validation Score: {score}")

# Task description
# Overview

## Description

As I scurried across the candlelit chamber, manuscripts in hand, I thought I'd made it. Nothing would be able to hurt me anymore. Little did I know there was one last fright lurking around the corner.

In this year's Halloween playground competition, you're challenged to predict the author of excerpts from horror stories by Edgar Allan Poe, Mary Shelley, and HP Lovecraft.

### Getting Started

New to Kernels or working with natural language data? We've put together some starter kernels in Python and R to help you hit the ground running.

## Evaluation

Submissions are evaluated using multi-class logarithmic loss. Each id has one true class. For each id, you must submit a predicted probability for each author. The formula is then:

$$\text{log loss} = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^M y_{ij} \log(p_{ij})$$

where N is the number of observations in the test set, M is the number of class labels (3 classes), \\(log\\) is the natural logarithm, \\(y_{ij}\\) is 1 if observation \\(i\\) belongs to class \\(j\\) and 0 otherwise, and \\(p_{ij}\\) is the predicted probability that observation \\(i\\) belongs to class \\(j\\).

The submitted probabilities for a given sentences are not required to sum to one because they are rescaled prior to being scored (each row is divided by the row sum). # MODEL DEFINITION: Hierarchical Attention Classifier
# ============================================================
class AttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
        self.attention_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(output_dim)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(output_dim, output_dim * 2),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 2, output_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        if input_dim != output_dim:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Linear(input_dim, output_dim)
        else:
            self.residual_proj = nn.Identity()

    def forward(self, x):
        attn_out = self.attention_proj(self.norm1(x))
        x = attn_out + self.residual_proj(x)
        ffn_out = self.ffn(self.norm2(x))
        x = ffn_out + x
        return x


class HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=3, dropout=0.15):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
        self.attention_block1 = AttentionBlock(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2, dropout)
        self.attention_block2 = AttentionBlock(
            hidden_dim // 2, hidden_dim // 4, dropout
        )
        self.attention_pool = nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 1)
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 4, 64),
            nn.LayerNorm(64),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout * 0.5),
            nn.Linear(64, num_classes),
        )
        self.apply(self._init_weights)

    def _init_weights(self, module):
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight, gain=1.0)
            if module.bias is not None:
                nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
            nn.init.constant_(module.bias, 0)
            nn.init.constant_(module.weight, 1.0)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.input_proj(x)
        x = self.attention_block1(x)
        x_attn = self.attention_block2(x)
        attention_weights = torch.softmax(self.attention_pool(x_attn), dim=1)
        x_weighted = x_attn * attention_weights
        logits = self.classifier(x_weighted)
        return logits


def create_model(num_classes=3):
    return HierarchicalAttentionClassifier(
        input_dim=768, hidden_dim=512, num_classes=num_classes, dropout=0.15
    )

# LOSS FUNCTION WITH LABEL SMOOTHING
# ============================================================
class LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, smoothing=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.smoothing = smoothing
        self.confidence = 1.0 - smoothing

    def forward(self, pred, target):
        log_probs = F.log_softmax(pred, dim=-1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            true_dist = torch.zeros_like(pred)
            true_dist.fill_(self.smoothing / (pred.size(-1) - 1))
            true_dist.scatter_(1, target.unsqueeze(1), self.confidence)
        return torch.mean(torch.sum(-true_dist * log_probs, dim=-1))


def get_criterion_and_optimizer(model, learning_rate=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01):
    criterion = LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy(smoothing=0.1)
    no_decay = ["bias", "LayerNorm.weight", "LayerNorm.bias", "norm"]
    optimizer_grouped_parameters = [
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if not any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": weight_decay,
        },
        {
            "params": [
                p
                for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                if any(nd in n for nd in no_decay)
            ],
            "weight_decay": 0.0,
        },
    ]
    optimizer = AdamW(
        optimizer_grouped_parameters, lr=learning_rate, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8
    )
    return criterion, optimizer

# MULTICLASS LOG LOSS

def multiclass_log_loss(y_true, y_pred_probs, eps=1e-15):
    y_pred_probs = np.clip(y_pred_probs, eps, 1 - eps)
    row_sums = y_pred_probs.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    y_pred_probs = y_pred_probs / row_sums
    y_true_one_hot = np.zeros_like(y_pred_probs)
    y_true_one_hot[np.arange(len(y_true)), y_true] = 1
    return -np.sum(y_true_one_hot * np.log(y_pred_probs)) / len(y_true)
